title: Quantization Bridge: fused-epilogue kernels and dynamic precision handoff for prefill/decode
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a small, focused runtime layer (Quantization Bridge) that minimizes data movement and dequant/requant overhead when switching between INT8/FP8 and FP32 execution paths during prefill and decode. The bridge will provide: (1) fused GEMM/epilogue kernels that incorporate quant-to-float scaling and optional bias/gelu/post-scaling without intermediate full-precision copies, (2) a compact dynamic-precision handoff policy that prefers lower precision during prefill and gracefully upgrades activations to higher precision for long-context attention or model-critical layers, and (3) scheduling primitives to co-locate conversions with KV prefill vs decode so we avoid redundant conversions for cached prefixes.

Context / Why this matters:
- Current per-token cost is dominated by repeated dequant->compute->requant cycles for mixed-precision checkpoints (esp. INT8 + FP8 experiments).
- Prefill phase does large batched matmuls where aggressive quant paths can yield 2-3x token throughput; decode must maintain low-latency single-token throughput without expensive memory copies.
- Existing kernels are fast in isolation but pay a high price in memory traffic and temporaries when the runtime stitches INT8/FP8 and float paths together.

Goals / success metrics:
- Reduce measured dequant/requant memory traffic by >= 60% on typical chat workloads (seq len 2048 prefill, decode 1) on A100/RTX8000 class nodes.
- Improve end-to-end prefill throughput on INT8 path by >= 1.8x vs today on our internal ResNet-like attention LLM bench.
- Keep 99th percentile decode latency increase <= 10% vs current FP32 baseline for single-token requests (target for model-constrained layers to fall back as needed).

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Fused-epilogue kernels: extend GEMM kernels to accept a quantized input+scale and perform dequant multiply-add inside the accumulation epilogue, applying bias, dropout (no-op for infer), and final output scaling without writing an intermediate FP32 tensor when the next operator supports a quantized consumer. This targets both INT8->FP32 and FP8->FP16 handoffs.
2) Shadow-weight FP8 storage: store a compact FP8 shadow of large feedforward weights for hot layers to enable purely quantized matmuls for prefill. We keep FP32/FP16 canonical weights for exact fallback and infrequent re-sync.
3) Dynamic precision handoff policy: runtime heuristic based on token age, KV reuse probability, and attention footprint. Prefill uses INT8/FP8 aggressive path; for decode, if attention window or layer sensitivity passes threshold, we insert an in-place upgrade fused kernel only for affected activations.
4) Cooperative scheduling for KV: schedule prefill conversions to align with KV layout so cached keys/values stay in the quantized format, and avoid conversion at decode time by reading quantized KV and using fused-epilogue kernels.
5) Micro-bench harness + golden prompt set: exhaustive microbench for GEMM/attention variants with memory counters to capture temporary allocations and copy counts.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Risk: fused kernels increase kernel combinatorial surface; we mitigate by a small matrix of supported operand types and a canonical fallback.
- Complexity: shadow FP8 weights add sync logic on model updates (handled in weight loader; lightweight).
- Correctness: FP8 path must be validated for regression on our eval suite to avoid silent quality regressions. We will tie to model-level regression alerts in Redwood Optimize.

Artifacts / links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood-internal/confluence/display/RUNTIME/Quantization+Bridge+Design
- Microbench dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood-internal/perf/quant-bridge
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5128 (WIP)
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end prefill throughput improvement >= 1.8x on the INT8 path measured on bench fixture; 2) Dequant/requant memory traffic reduced >= 60% measured by allocator counters; 3) No quality regression for a curated prompt set (diff metrics within +/-1% BLEU/ROUGE/LL loss thresholds depending on model family) or explicit sign-off from Applied ML; 4) Feature flagged rollout with automatic fallback to FP32 per-request when errors or anomalies are detected.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for fused-epilogue kernel correctness across quant/float type combos.
- Microbench (batch sizes: 1, 8, 32) for prefill and decode; compare with baseline kernels and collect allocation/copy metrics.
- Integration test: run end-to-end serving with KV caching enabled on dedicated pool, validate decode p99 latency.
- Offline quality eval: run eval-suite (prompt set: quant-bridge-gold) and ensure scores meet acceptance criteria.
- Backwards compatibility test: model load/unload with shadow weight resync on rolling upgrade.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature gated behind 'quant_bridge' runtime flag in config.
2) Canary: enable on 5% of internal perf tenants with non-sensitive workloads and monitor perf/quality.
3) Expand to Dedicated pools with opt-in 'quant-bridge' tuning presets.
4) Default enable for supported models after two cycles of canary with stable metrics.
5) Emergency off switch mapped to circuit-breaker in Console and API-level compatibility mode.
